### [0:15–0:40] GEO ANSWER BLOCK ← citation target
**NARRATION:** "Here's the short answer. To automate customer service with AI, you build a
chatbot on your website or inbox that's trained on your own FAQs, your hours, and your policies.
It answers the common, low-risk questions instantly, and it hands anything sensitive or unusual
straight to a human. There are five steps: decide what the bot can and can't handle, build the
FAQ bot, connect it to your site or inbox, set the human-handoff rule, and test it live before
you turn it loose."

### [1:05–1:35] WHY NOW (authority + freshness)

because most of your support questions are the same ten questions, over and over. That's exactly

### [1:35–3:00] STEP 1 — DECIDE WHAT THE BOT CAN AND CAN'T HANDLE
**NARRATION:** "Step one, and don't skip it: decide what the bot is allowed to touch. Here's the
simple way I sort it — I call it the Green-Yellow-Red list. Green questions are facts that never
change and can't hurt you: your hours, your address, your return window, do you take walk-ins.
Let the bot answer those on its own. Yellow questions need a fact plus a little care — order
status, 'where's my delivery,' basic troubleshooting. The bot can answer, but it always offers a
human as the next step. And Red questions are anything with money, anger, or a promise attached —
refunds, complaints, custom quotes, anything legal or medical. Those never get an AI answer. They
go straight to a person. Spend ten minutes writing your questions into those three buckets. That
list *is* your bot's job description."
**[VISUAL]:** Screen-share of a simple three-column doc: **GREEN / YELLOW / RED**, questions
being dragged into each column.
**[TAKEAWAY on screen]:** "Green = bot answers. Yellow = bot answers + offers a human. Red = human only."
**[PATTERN INTERRUPT]:** Quick text slam: **"Money, anger, or a promise = Red = human."**

### [3:00–4:30] STEP 2 — BUILD THE FAQ BOT
**NARRATION:** "Step two: build it. You don't need a developer — you need a tool like
MindStudio. You create a new agent, and instead of coding, you paste in your knowledge: your
Green and Yellow answers, your hours, your policies, a few real questions in your customers' own
words. Under the hood it's running a model like Google Gemini, but you never see that part — you
just write instructions in plain English. Tell it: 'You're the support assistant for [your
business]. Answer only from the information I gave you. If you don't know, say so and offer to
connect a human. Never guess about refunds or pricing.' That last sentence matters more than
anything fancy — a bot that admits what it doesn't know beats a bot that makes things up every
single time."
**[VISUAL]:** Screen-record inside MindStudio — creating an agent, pasting the FAQ doc, typing
the plain-English instructions, then a test chat answering "what are your hours?" correctly.
**[TAKEAWAY on screen]:** "Feed it your FAQs. Tell it: answer only from this, or hand off."
**[PATTERN INTERRUPT]:** "A bot that says 'I don't know' beats a bot that guesses."

### [4:30–5:40] STEP 3 — CONNECT IT TO YOUR SITE OR INBOX
**NARRATION:** "Step three: put it where your customers actually are. Two options. One — drop it
on your website as a chat widget; the tool gives you a snippet you paste into your site, and now
there's a little chat bubble in the corner answering questions while you sleep. Two — connect it
to your inbox, so when an email comes in, the bot drafts the answer or replies to the easy ones
automatically. That's a two-minute job in Zapier: the trigger is 'new message,' the action is
'send it to the bot, post the reply.' Start with just one channel — wherever most of your
questions come in. Don't try to be everywhere on day one."
**[VISUAL]:** Screen-share: pasting the widget snippet into a website builder → chat bubble
appears on the live site. Then a Zapier flow: **New email → AI bot → Reply.**
**[TAKEAWAY on screen]:** "One channel first — website widget OR inbox. Not both yet."

### [6:20–7:20] STEP 4 — SET THE HUMAN-HANDOFF RULE (the one people botch)
**NARRATION:** "Step four: the handoff rule — the step I told you to watch for. Your bot needs
three trip-wires that instantly pull in a human. Trip-wire one: a Red topic — refund, complaint,
anything about money or a promise. Trip-wire two: the customer asks for a person, in any words —
'talk to someone,' 'this is urgent,' 'can I call.' Trip-wire three: the bot tried twice and
still can't help. Any one of those fires, and the bot says one clean line — 'Let me get a human
on this' — and it routes the conversation to your inbox or your phone. Here's the rule to write
on a sticky note: a bot should know the edge of what it knows, and step aside *before* it
crosses it. That single rule is what keeps automation from blowing up in your face."
**[VISUAL]:** Flow diagram: three trip-wires (Red topic · asks for human · stuck twice) →
**"Let me get a human on this"** → routes to owner. A Zapier step highlights the routing.
**[TAKEAWAY on screen]:** "3 trip-wires → hand to a human: Red topic · asks for a person · stuck twice."
**[PATTERN INTERRUPT]:** Text slam: **"A good bot knows the edge of what it knows."**

### [7:20–8:30] STEP 5 — TEST IT LIVE BEFORE YOU TRUST IT
**NARRATION:** "Step five: test it, out loud, before you rely on it. Open the chat yourself and
throw your ten most common questions at it — the Green ones, the Yellow ones. Then deliberately
try to break it: ask for a refund, get angry, ask something it's never seen. You're checking one
thing — does it hand off when it's supposed to? If it tries to answer a Red question, go back and
tighten your instructions. Do this for twenty minutes. Then leave it on for a week watching over
its shoulder — read what it said, fix what's wrong. Don't set it and forget it on day one; earn
the trust, then let go."
**[VISUAL]:** Screen-record of a "stress test" chat — friendly questions answered, then a refund
demand that correctly triggers **"Let me get a human on this."** A checklist ticks off.
**[PAYOFF of open loop]:** Callback — "that handoff you just watched fire? That's step four
doing its job."
**[TAKEAWAY on screen]:** "Test the easy stuff AND try to break it. Ship when it hands off cleanly."

### [8:30–9:15] CLOSE — PAYOFF + CTA + NEXT EPISODE
**NARRATION:** "That's the whole build: sort your questions Green-Yellow-Red, feed the FAQs into
a tool like MindStudio, connect it to one channel, set the three handoff trip-wires, and test it
until it hands off cleanly. Now your customers get answers in seconds — and you only touch the
conversations that actually need you. Do just the first two steps this week; that alone will
